scenarios: Constitutional accommodation with legally accepted oaths, tenure and rulings
Prolonged parallel legal authority under functioning elections and ministries
Broader unconstitutional coercive rupture beyond a single judicial institution
Severe eastern-frontier security or hybrid shock requiring NATO coordination
contrary_evidence: Reuters and AP document contested court suspension and police intervention; neither establishes a completed military overthrow or replacement national government.
The Polish president's interrupted Senegal trip demonstrates political alarm but does not by itself mean the army seized state power.
March–April 2026 disputed parliamentary and presidential judicial oaths predate the October standoff; the crisis is not uniquely explained by foreign interference.
EU funding conditionality and Poland's earlier judicial conflicts are real but do not establish that Brussels ordered the October 30 police operation.
Russian UAV incursions and hybrid activity establish security risks, not proof that Moscow directed the Tribunal confrontation.
Commission 2026 real GDP growth forecast of 3.5% means political and fiscal instability cannot be equated with observed recession.
Poland remains in the EU but retains the zloty; the Commission 2026 convergence assessment does not identify euro accession as completed.
Polish–Ukrainian strategic cooperation coexists with genuine economic and historical disputes; disagreement does not demonstrate Russian control over all opposition voices.
NATO 7 July 2026 comparable data put Poland fourth, after Lithuania, Estonia and Latvia; the r1 NATO first-place description was a source-vintage error corrected in r2.
EU Commission's year-on-year GDP and HICP percentage growth rates have different denominators than deficit and debt as shares of GDP; these are now depicted in separate charts.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 30 October 2026; NATO Defence Investment Update 7 July 2026 is the controlling comparable defence ranking for 2026. European Commission spring May 2026 forecast distinguishes GDP/HICP year-on-year rates from deficit and debt % GDP. Political news October 30, 2026.
producer_checks.research_depth: 35 numbered chapters per locale, approximately 8,285 PT-BR and 7,132 EN whitespace-delimited words including chart values and 32 source entries; substantive historical, constitutional, EU political economy, NATO-Russia-Ukraine, and conditional future analysis.
producer_checks.source_check: 32 same numbered URLs per locale; new primary NATO July 7 2026 source [32] verifies 2026 Poland fourth at 4.68%, with Lithuania 5.33, Estonia 5.10, Latvia 4.92. EC May 2026 source [5] supports GDP, HICP and deficit chart split. Some prior sources overlap (PISM [13] and [30]) and are retained for attribution; independent QA may review.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Five matching quantitative bar charts per locale: (1) GDP growth/HICP year-on-year 3.6,3.5,2.8,3.6%; (2) deficit absolute magnitude as % GDP 7.3,6.5,6.3; (3) gross debt % GDP 59.7,64.5,68.3; (4) OECD/IMF defence trend 2.2,4.5,4.8,5.0% GDP (vintages distinguished); (5) NATO comparable 2026 expenditure Lithuania 5.33, Estonia 5.10, Latvia 4.92, Poland 4.68% GDP. Two paired evidence tables, one institutional flow, one geography map, one mindmap in each locale.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 35 matching numbered chapters, 32 identical bibliography URLs, identical five chart numerical series and chart/flow/map/mindmap order; explanatory distinctions about NATO 2026 vs OECD/IMF older estimates and annual rates vs GDP denominator made in both languages.
producer_checks.methodology: Distinguishes reported court suspension and legal claims from adjudicated validity; democratic institutional deadlock from completed military coup; documented EU conditionality and NATO integration from unverified external orchestration; forecasts from observed values; NATO defence spending methodology from fiscal accounts; Russian hybrid risks from proof of complicity in Polish judicial proceedings.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Revision 2 resubmitted for fresh independent QA, after specific r1 factual and units errors fixed. All staged blobs updated and source Git SHAs pinned. No independent approval or public publication yet.
producer_checks.qa_handoff: Verify both r1 blockers specifically: no highest-in-NATO 2026 claim, NATO July 7 link [32], 2026 4.68% fourth, 2025 and OECD projection vintages separated; charts with common units only, GDP/HICP YoY chart separate from general government deficit (% GDP), fifth NATO comparison chart matched across languages. Independently verify exact source Git SHAs and no unsupported coup or foreign-orchestration claims.

revision_reason: Corrects the independent QA rejection of r1: NATO 7 July 2026 comparable ranking has Lithuania 5.33%, Estonia 5.10%, Latvia 4.92% and Poland 4.68% (fourth); separates GDP/HICP annual percent-change visual from deficit levels (% GDP). Adds 32nd primary NATO source; both language versions, figures and evidence updated.
